chunks: And command the people of Mecca not to take rent from a lodger, for indeed Allah, Glorified is He, says: 'Alike [are] the one who stays [in the mosque] and the one who is outside.'

key_terms.الْعَاكِفُ: The one who stays/dwells (often used for i'tikaf or permanent residence)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on charging rent to pilgrims in Mecca according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) instructs the governor of Mecca to exempt residents from lodging fees, citing Quran 22:25 to highlight the spiritual equality between the permanent dweller (al-'akif) and the traveler (al-badid) within the sacred precincts. This directive underscores the principle of accessibility and hospitality in the holy city, ensuring that economic barriers do not hinder the spiritual presence of all believers, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the sanctity of Mecca's spaces.
